Released: 19 November 2026

EDB Postgres Distributed 5.10.0 includes an enhancement and bug fixes focused on improving stability and reliability. For a list of known issues, see [Known issues and limitations](/pgd/5.10/known_issues/).

## Enhancements

<table class="table w-100"><thead><tr><th>Component</th><th>Version</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>BDR</td><td>5.10.0</td><td><details><summary>Backported Raft <a href="/pgd/5.10/routing/raft/04_raft_elections_in_depth/#raft-leader-elections-and-prevote">PreVote</a> from PGD 6 to prevent unnecessary Raft leader elections.</summary><p>A node that was isolated by a flapping network link no longer forces a Raft leader election when it reconnects. Before it starts a real election, a node now asks the other voting nodes whether they would vote for it, without raising its term. An isolated node can't gather a majority, so it doesn't depose a healthy leader on its return. PreVote needs no configuration. It takes effect once all nodes run PGD 5.10 and the group negotiates Raft protocol version 5011. In PGD 5.10.0, PreVote applies to the Raft instance of the top-level group only.</p>
</details></td></tr>
</tbody></table>


## Bug Fixes

<table class="table w-100"><thead><tr><th>Component</th><th>Version</th><th>Description</th><th width="10%">Addresses</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>BDR</td><td>5.10.0</td><td><details><summary>Fixed a hard hang between a writer and the receiver in CAMO.</summary><p>A receiver restart, for example after the origin node was partitioned and then recovered, could hang when the downstream node had CAMO transactions in its commit decisions. The receiver waited on a flush while the writers waited for the full commit decision feedback queues that the receiver never emptied. The deadlock detector didn't detect this hang, and only a server restart resolved it. This issue has been present since 5.9.1.</p>
</details></td><td>65610</td></tr>
<tr><td>BDR</td><td>5.10.0</td><td><details><summary>Fixed the receiver skipping cleanup when it exits with a broken upstream connection.</summary><p>When a receiver exited gracefully while its upstream connection was already broken, sending standby status or CAMO feedback raised an <code>ERROR</code> inside the exit callback. That unwound out of the finish function and skipped writer cleanup, closing the connection, and the remaining exit callbacks. During process exit, these failures are now logged as warnings and the cleanup runs to completion.</p>
</details></td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>BDR</td><td>5.10.0</td><td><details><summary>Lag values in <code>bdr.node_slots</code> are no longer reset when a peer reconnects.</summary><p>During the catch-up phase, the <code>write_lag</code>, <code>flush_lag</code>, and <code>replay_lag</code> fields in <code>bdr.node_slots</code> now report the calculated <code>offline_lag</code> until the slot goes back to the streaming state and lag can be measured again, instead of being reset to 0.</p>
</details></td><td>57149</td></tr>
<tr><td>BDR</td><td>5.10.0</td><td><details><summary>Prevented DDL from creating galloc sequences with the <code>CYCLE</code> option.</summary><p>The <code>CYCLE</code> option on galloc sequences could cause duplicate <code>nextval()</code> values across nodes. PGD now prevents DDL that results in a galloc sequence with the <code>CYCLE</code> option, unless it's replicated DDL from another node.</p>
</details></td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>PGD CLI</td><td>5.10.0</td><td><details><summary>PGD CLI now honors <code>ssl_password_command</code> from its configuration file.</summary><p>The <code>cluster.ssl.ssl_password_command</code> setting in <code>pgd-cli-config.yml</code> was accepted but ignored, so an obfuscated <code>sslpassword</code> failed with &quot;bad decrypt&quot; for users without a libpq deobfuscation preload, such as <code>root</code>. The CLI again runs the command with <code>sslpassword</code> on standard input and uses its output as the passphrase. Passwords are no longer shown in <code>--debug</code> output.</p>
</details></td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>BDR</td><td>5.10.0</td><td><details><summary>Fixed an assertion failure on subtransaction order in file-streamed transactions.</summary><p>The receiver asserted that the subtransactions of a transaction streamed to a file are in XID order. They are added in the order of their first change, which can differ, so the receiver crashed on assert-enabled builds. The receiver no longer checks the XID order and only checks that positions in the changes file increase.</p>
</details></td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>
